Q: How to GROUP BY one column with SELECT * A:

Sorry if my answer is not grammatically correct, English is not my native language.

You have to put the arguments in the proper order.

Link

I don't know what type of columns you have in the table, and what results you want to get. I mean, I don't know if you want to count() or sum() a column.

I have understood in your post that you only want to see the results in which 'payout=0'.

For example, With the information you provided, I would do the following:

SELECT * FROM data dt LEFT JOIN payment pm ON pm.month = dt.month AND pm.persID = dt.persID where pm.payout = 0 GROUP BY dt.department;

Q: How Can I Exclude Holidays Using My Custom Holiday Table Into my SQL Code that Excludes Weekends A:

Count business days between the two dates instead, then compare to 3. That handles weekends and holidays with the same logic.

SELECT c.ContactID, c.ContactType, c.ContactDate,
       CASE WHEN c.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
             AND bd.BusinessDays <= 3
            THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No'
       END AS Day3Validate
FROM dbo.Contacts c
OUTER APPLY (
    SELECT MIN(ContactDate) AS Type1Date
    FROM dbo.Contacts t1
    WHERE t1.ContactID = c.ContactID AND t1.ContactType = 'TYPE1'
) T1
OUTER APPLY (
    SELECT MIN(ContactDate) AS Type2Date
    FROM dbo.Contacts t2
    WHERE t2.ContactID = c.ContactID AND t2.ContactType = 'TYPE2'
) T2
OUTER APPLY (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS BusinessDays
    FROM dbo.Calendar cal
    WHERE cal.TheDate > T1.Type1Date
      AND cal.TheDate <= T2.Type2Date
      AND DATEPART(WEEKDAY, cal.TheDate) NOT IN (1, 7)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.Holidays h WHERE h.HolidayDate = cal.TheDate)
) bd

You'll also need a calendar table, which you can generate like below. Also note DATEPART(WEEKDAY, ...) depends on DATEFIRST, so hardcoding 1 and 7 for Sunday and Saturday breaks if that setting changes

OUTER APPLY (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS BusinessDays
    FROM (SELECT TOP (DATEDIFF(DAY, T1.Type1Date, T2.Type2Date))
                 DATEADD(DAY, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)), T1.Type1Date) AS d
          FROM sys.all_objects) x
    WHERE DATEPART(WEEKDAY, x.d) NOT IN (1, 7)
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.Holidays h WHERE h.HolidayDate = x.d)
) bd

Q: how to build automation tabchi bot A:

A quick internet search reveals the Python 3 library python-telegram-bot, with documentation available at https://python-telegram-bot.org/. Using this library's asynchronous abstractions of the Telegram Bot API, alongside some simple infinite event looping with asyncio.sleep in the middle (asyncio is a built-in library, so you won't need to install it), you should quite easily be able to construct a Telegram bot that sends messages at scheduled intervals.

The following code—or some variation upon it—should be sufficient, assuming your needs are strictly to message some hardcoded channel at a hardcoded interval. There are plenty of changes to be made, so consider this a jumping-off point, not a finished product:

import asyncio
import telegram

async def main():
    bot = telegram.Bot("your token goes here")
    async with bot:
        while True:
            await bot.send_message(text="some message", chat_id=123456)
            await asyncio.sleep(100) # Input in seconds

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Q: FileNotFound exception in Java/Clojure interop A:

The console output above your stacktrace shows the classpath that Java is being invoked with. Most of them are libraries cached from the Maven repository, plus intellij's own runtime jar, idea_rt.jar. The only entry that's a part of your intellij project is the first one, C:\Users\Joe User\IdeaProjects\chit260731\out\production\Listening. This path clearly has no relation to your project.clj at all, since you don't mention the out\production path. So your intellij launch configuration is just wrong.

I'm not familiar with setting up Clojure projects in intellij so I can't give further advice any better than "google how to set up leiningen projects in intellij". But I can say, whatever you need to do is in the intellij menus. You can't solve your problem by editing any of your source files, including project.clj.

Q: how to add a "needs" based on a condition A:

Edit: Gitlab added a rules:needs: syntax in version 16.1, so you can now use the exact syntax OP guessed in the question.

test:sauce:
  # ...
  rules:
  - if: "$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH" != "master"
    needs: ['review']

Previous answer, for posterity

On Gitlab <16.1, there's another workaround for this in the form of the needs:optional syntax

If the 'review' job only exists on the branch of interest, you can mark it as "optional" and gitlab will ignore the fact that it doesn't exist on pipelines on other branches.

test:sauce:
 # ...
 needs:
 - job: 'review'
   optional: true

If the 'review' job exists unconditionally, you can make a dummy job that only exists on the branch.

review_on_master:
  needs: ['review']
  variables:
    GIT_STRATEGY: none
  script: ['true']
  rules:
  - if: "$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH" != "master"
    when: never

test:sauce:
 # ...
 needs:
 - job: 'review_on_master'
   optional: true
